source_text: Quam unitatem firmiter tenere et vindicare debemus, maxime episcopi, qui in Ecclesia praesidemus, ut episcopatum quoque ipsum unum atque indivisum probemus. Nemo fraternitatem mendacio fallat, nemo fidei veritatem perfida praevaricatione corrumpat. Episcopatus unus est, cujus a singulis in solidum pars tenetur. Ecclesia quoque una est, quae in multitudinem latius incremento foecunditatis extenditur. Quomodo solis multi radii, sed lumen unum; et rami arboris multi, sed robur unum tenaci radice fundatum; et cum de fonte uno rivi plurimi defluunt, numerositas licet diffusa videatur exundantis copiae largitate, unitas tamen servatur in origine. Avelle radium solis a corpore, divisionem lucis unitas non capit: ab arbore frange ramum, fractus germinare non poterit: a fronte praecide rivum, praecisus arescit. Sic et Ecclesia Domini luce perfusa per orbem totum radios suos porrigit; unum tamen lumen est, quod ubique diffunditur, nec unitas corporis separatur. Ramos suos in universam terram copia ubertatis extendit, profluentes largiter rivos latius expandit; unum tamen caput est et origo una, et una mater foecunditatis successibus copiosa. Illius foetu nascimur, illius lacte nutrimur, spiritu ejus animamur.
pass_a_gloss: Which unity we ought to hold and vindicate firmly, especially we bishops, who preside in the Church, so that we may also prove the episcopate itself to be one and indivisible. Let no one deceive the brotherhood with a lie, let no one corrupt the truth of the faith with a perfidious prevarication. The episcopate is one, of which a part is held in solidum by individuals. The Church is also one, which is extended more widely into a multitude by the increment of fecundity. Just as many rays of the sun, but one light; and many branches of a tree, but one trunk founded on a tenacious root; and when many streams flow from one spring, although the multitude may seem to be diffused by the largesse of the overflowing abundance, yet unity is preserved in the origin. To tear a ray from the body of the sun, unity does not admit of a division of light: to break a branch from a tree, the broken branch will not be able to germinate: to cut a stream from its source, the cut stream will dry up. So also the Church of the Lord, filled with light, extends its rays throughout the whole world; yet the light is one, which is diffused everywhere, and the unity of the body is not separated. It extends its branches into the whole earth with an abundance of fertility, it expands more widely the flowing streams with a generous largesse; yet there is one head and one origin, and one mother of fertility, rich in successes. We are born of her womb, we are nourished by her milk, we are animated by her Spirit.
pass_b_english: We must hold and defend this unity firmly, especially we bishops who preside over the Church, so that we may also prove that the episcopate itself is one and indivisible. No one is to deceive the brotherhood with a lie, and no one is to corrupt the truth of the faith with a faithless violation. The episcopate is one, and each bishop holds it in its entirety. The Church is also one, spreading wider into a multitude through the increase of her fruitfulness. Just as the sun has many rays but only one light, and a tree has many branches but one trunk rooted in a tenacious root, and many streams flow from a single spring — though the multitude may seem scattered by the generosity of its overflowing abundance, unity is still preserved at the source. If you tear a ray from the body of the sun, unity does not allow a division of light; if you break a branch from a tree, the broken branch cannot sprout; if you cut a stream from its source, the severed stream dries up. So too the Church of the Lord, filled with light, extends her rays throughout the whole world; yet the light is one, diffused everywhere, and the unity of the body is not divided. She spreads her branches over the whole earth with an abundance of fruitfulness, and her flowing streams expand widely with generous bounty; yet there is one head, one origin, and one mother of fruitfulness, rich in offspring. We are born from her womb, nourished by her milk, and given life by her Spirit.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the legal/technical phrase 'in solidum' (Pass A via gloss, Pass B via 'in its entirety') and the theological imagery of the sun, tree, and spring. The distinction between 'foecunditas' as fecundity/fruitfulness is maintained. All clauses, including the conditional 'if/to' structures in the middle of the paragraph, are preserved in sense and agency.
